labels.label: T-loc-flat-time-cylinder/1-topology
labels.notes: The model is the one in the evidence. Printed: Causal.Minkowski = fun n => ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), so the first coordinate is time (minkowski_lt_top_iff: ‖q.2 − p.2‖ < q.1 − p.1). FlatQuotient.timeVec d = (1, 0) = e₀. timeTranslation n acts by AffineEquiv.constVAdd (n • timeVec), and timeGroup d is its range. TimeCylinder d is the reducible abbrev FlatQuotient (timeGroup d) ⊤ = MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient (timeGroup d) ⊤, with the quotient topology and the library's charted structure (FlatQuotient.instHasGroupoid). timeCylinder d is the reducible abbrev flatCausality d (TimeCylinder d). So this is ℤe₀\𝐌ⁿ, and Barbot's n = d + 1 is stated in the docstring (kb/0024). T2 is timeCylinder_t2Space (the theorem FlatQuotient.t2Space, whose instance is mathlib's, from the library's ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul and IsCancelSMul instances on timeGroup). Connected is the global instance TimeCylinder.instConnectedSpace. Second countable is the global instance TimeCylinder.instSecondCountableTopology, from flat_secondCountableTopology (DEC-49). Neither instance takes a hypothesis. Three Prop-valued global instances sit on the abbrev: these two, and CompactSpace (TimeCylinder 0). They are harmless, and the REPORT discloses them.

labels.label: T-loc-flat-time-cylinder/2-ladder
labels.notes: Layer-3 rule satisfied. A metaprogram read the head constant of every conjunct of timeCylinder_separates, timeCylinder_zero_separates and each single theorem. Each head is exactly the `lean` field of programme/ladder.toml: Causal.Causality.CurvesExtend, Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal (reached by dot notation through toPrecausality), Causal.Causality.CausallyArcConnected, .PushUp, .Tarentin, .ChronalNeighbours, .CausallyOpen and .CausallyPlain, each applied to (TimeCylinder d, its quotient topology, timeCylinder d). #print of the compiled definitions agrees with the ladder's `what` lines: CausallyOpen is the two-sided form of DEC-8, and ChronalNeighbours is ChronalPastNeighbours ∧ dual.ChronalPastNeighbours. None of the eight takes a hypothesis, and all hold for every d. So the abstract theorems apply without restatement. One step is checked by causal_ladder: causally_open from push_up ∧ chronal_neighbours, by the rule PushUp.causallyOpen_of_chronalNeighbours (Causal/Ladder/Rules.lean:42). The other derived steps cite their lemmas, as the REPORT says. Chronal neighbours come from AbsolutelyMinimal.chronalNeighbours_iff_Z (ChronalNeighbourBridge.lean:196, T1), with Z± = univ from flat_singularFlatAxioms with empty singular set. causally_plain comes from PushUp.causallyPlain_of_chronalNeighbours (CausallyPlainLocZ.lean:202), which has no standing hypothesis. The Rules file has no plainness rule from push-up ∧ chronal neighbours, so the docstring's 'plainness is not yet a rule' is true. SingularFlatAxioms.causallyPlain (Causal/SingularFlatPlain.lean:90) does take (hSC : C.StronglyCausal), and the cylinder is not strongly causal, so the SCOPE's reason for not using it is true. The extra negations also use the ladder's definitions: StronglyCausal, StronglyCausalOpen, HasTimeFunction, GloballyHyperbolic.

labels.label: T-loc-flat-time-cylinder/3-not-causal
labels.notes: timeCylinder_not_isCausal : ∀ {d}, ¬ (timeCylinder d).IsCausal, where IsCausal is antisymmetry of le ⊤ (def:causal_spacetime, ETT.tex:653–655; the quote is verbatim). The stronger result is timeCylinder_lt_top : ∀ {d} (x y : TimeCylinder d), (timeCylinder d).lt ⊤ x y, so the whole space is totally vicious. Its argument is sound. It lifts x to a and y to b and picks n with ‖b₂ − a₂‖ < n + b₁ − a₁. In 𝐌ⁿ this gives a ≪ n e₀ + b, and strongMorphism_proj carries that to the quotient, where [n e₀ + b] = [b] (timeCylinder_proj_shift). Because ≪_M relates every pair, each failure in the REPORT's list holds and follows by the existing edges: not strongly causal (StronglyCausal.isCausal, T1), not StronglyCausalOpen, no time function, and not globally hyperbolic.

labels.label: T-loc-flat-time-cylinder/4-not-causally-compact
labels.notes: Reading 'd ≥ 1 space dimensions' as (hd : 1 ≤ d) on Minkowski d is right (kb/0024): Minkowski d = ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), so d is the spatial dimension. Only timeCylinder_not_compactSpace, timeCylinder_not_causallyCompact and timeCylinder_separates take hd. The rest of the file holds for every d. timeCylinder_diamond shows diamond ⊤ p q = univ, using the diamond J⁻{q} ∩ J⁺{p} of def:causally_compact. So CausallyCompact ↔ CompactSpace (TimeCylinder d). For 1 ≤ d, ‖a₂‖ descends by Quotient.lift to a continuous function that is unbounded at the class of (0, single ⟨0, hd⟩ (|R|+1)), so the cylinder is not compact. timeCylinder_causallyCompact_iff : (timeCylinder d).CausallyCompact ↔ d = 0, so the hypothesis is sharp. For d = 0, TimeCylinder.instCompactSpaceZero holds because the cylinder is the image of the slab Icc 0 1 × univ, with 𝐑⁰ a subsingleton. The quote of def:causally_compact (ETT.tex:350–352) is its second sentence, verbatim.

labels.label: T-loc-flat-time-cylinder/5-separation
labels.notes: timeCylinder_separates (hd : 1 ≤ d) prints as (T2Space ∧ SecondCountableTopology ∧ ConnectedSpace) ∧ CurvesExtend ∧ AbsolutelyMinimal ∧ CausallyArcConnected ∧ PushUp ∧ Tarentin ∧ ChronalNeighbours ∧ CausallyOpen ∧ CausallyPlain ∧ ¬ IsCausal ∧ ¬ CausallyCompact, all at timeCylinder d. This is exactly for_keeper.fails[0] and [1]: `from` is the eight ids, `to` is is_causal or causally_compact, and T2 and second countability are conjuncts. timeCylinder_zero_separates prints as (T2 ∧ SC ∧ Connected ∧ CompactSpace) ∧ the same eight ∧ CausallyCompact ∧ ¬ IsCausal at timeCylinder 0. This is exactly fails[2], whose `from` is causally_compact plus the eight. It is a genuine Hausdorff, second-countable witness of causally_compact ⇏ is_causal. The OQ-18 claim is true. absolutely_minimal is a conjunct, so the separations hold in the gluing reading. They also hold in the stricter hereditary reading: an example under `import Causal` checks (timeCylinder d).AbsolutelyMinimalOn W for every open W, by Causal.Flat.flatCausality_absolutelyMinimalOn (Causal/Flat/FlatSpacetime.lean:156). Ladder simulation on /tmp copies, using tools/ladder.py's refuted(); programme/ladder.toml is unmodified since a45528d. With `space` absent, the two cylinder entries settle exactly 50 [[open]] pairs and nothing else moves. Without causally_plain in `from` they settle 44, and the 6 extra pairs are causally_plain → {causally_compact, globally_hyperbolic, is_causal, strongly_causal, strongly_causal_open, time_function}. The REPORT's list of 50 and all its line numbers match. The circle entry settles 5 more, at :1647, :1652, :2218, :2295 and :2384 (causally_compact → is_causal, globally_hyperbolic, strongly_causal, strongly_causal_open, time_function), as the REPORT lists. The dispatch cites :1636 among the circle's lines, but :1636 is curves_extend → time_function, which the cylinder settles (it is in cylinder_50), not the circle. The REPORT is right there. The open count goes 150 → 95. `ladder.py check --file` on the extended copy reports only the 3 'witness not found' violations expected before graduation, with no contradiction. With the file placed at Causal/Model/FlatTimeCylinder.lean in a temp root, lean_index resolves Causal.Flat.timeCylinder_separates and Causal.Flat.timeCylinder_zero_separates. The is_causal entry alone carries 49 of the 50. The roadmap evidence's '48 of the 50' is the planner's figure, not the closer's, and is off by one: only causally_plain → causally_compact needs the second entry.

findings.what: The proposed [[fails]] entries say `"space": []` while their `space_note` says 'absent'. tools/ladder.py's space() reads a present empty list as the empty space (vocab_closure([])), not the ambient. So a literal transcription chains only the edges with no standing hypothesis. Simulated: the two cylinder entries would then settle 26 [[open]] pairs instead of 50, and 29 instead of 55 with the circle. The REPORT's own simulation, with `space` absent, is correct. The entries also carry `space_note`, `reading` and `optional`, which are not [[fails]] keys (KEYS['fails'] = from, to, witness, status, space), so `ladder.py check` would reject them as unknown keys if copied. Other REPORTs (e.g. T-abs-pushup-of-minimal-local) omit `space` when the witness is one of ETT's spacetimes.
findings.fix: For the keeper: record the three entries with no `space` key, and move space_note, reading and optional into a comment or the master's journal. Optionally, for the closer: drop `"space": []` from for_keeper.fails.
